title: 387. The Fall of the Aztecs: Prisoners of Montezuma (Part 4)

sentences.en: That night, as Hernan Cortes stood on his balcony and stared out across the lights of the city, his mind was uneasy.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，当埃尔南·科尔特斯站在阳台上，凝视着这座城市的点点灯火时，他的内心并不平静。

sentences.en: To seek his fortune, he had travelled thousands of miles across land and sea, and here he was, in the centre of an island city, in the heart of a foreign empire,
sentences.zh: 为了寻求财富，他历经千难万险跨越海陆，而此刻，他竟身处一座海岛城市中央，身处一个异国帝国的腹地，

sentences.en: surrounded by people who didn't speak his language, didn't worship his god, and could turn on him at any moment.
sentences.zh: 周围的人不会说他的语言，不信仰他的神明，并且随时可能调转枪头对付他。

sentences.en: And as a deep silence fell across the city, one thought prayed on his mind.
sentences.zh: 当一片死寂笼罩这座城市时，一个念头折磨着他的心。

sentences.en: So far, he had been lucky, but one day, very soon, his luck might run out.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他一直很幸运，但用不了多久，他的好运可能就要耗尽了。

sentences.en: Thrilling stuff there, Dominic, from your new book, The Fall of the Aztecs, one of your Adventures in Time series.
sentences.zh: 讲得太精彩了，多米尼克，这段出自你的新书《阿兹特克帝国的衰落》，也就是你的“时间冒险”系列之一。

sentences.en: Great stuff.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And we are, what is this, I'm losing track, episode four?
sentences.zh: 我们这是到第几集了，我都记不清了，第四集吗？

sentences.en: Episode four, Tom.
sentences.zh: 第四集，汤姆。

sentences.en: Into our Aztec epic, and Cortes and his Spanish adventurers are in Tenochtitlan, the great Aztec capital, and what is going to happen next?
sentences.zh: 进入我们的阿兹特克史诗，科尔特斯和他的西班牙探险家们来到了特诺奇蒂特兰，这座伟大的阿兹特克首都，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, this is the question, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是问题所在，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: Because this thought must have been on their minds.
sentences.zh: 因为这个念头肯定一直在他们脑海中萦绕。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, how could it not be?
sentences.zh: 对啊，我的意思是，怎么可能没有呢？

sentences.en: Cortes, just to recap, has made this extraordinary gamble.
sentences.zh: 我们回顾一下，科尔特斯进行了一场非同寻常的豪赌。

sentences.en: He has gone against his orders with this company, many of whom are probably not particularly loyal to him and have their own agendas.
sentences.zh: 他违背了命令，带着这支队伍深入此地，其中许多人可能对他并不忠诚，各有各的小算盘。

sentences.en: They have gone inland, as we discussed last time.
sentences.zh: 正如我们上次讨论的那样，他们已经深入内陆。

sentences.en: They seem to have struck this alliance with a city-state called Tlaxcala.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎与一个叫特拉斯卡拉的城邦结成了同盟。

sentences.en: And then they've gone across the causeway.
sentences.zh: 然后他们穿过了堤道。

sentences.en: They've been welcomed by the Mexica, by their emperor, Montezuma, or Moctezuma, or whatever one might call him.
sentences.zh: 他们受到了墨西加人、他们的皇帝蒙特苏马（或莫克索苏马，随你怎么叫他）的欢迎。

sentences.en: And they've been welcomed.
sentences.zh: 而且他们受到了热烈欢迎。

sentences.en: They've been installed in the palace, in the center of the kind of big ceremonial temple quarter.
sentences.zh: 他们被安置在宫殿里，位于大型宗教神庙区的中心地带。

sentences.en: And what is going on?
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: I mean, the truth of the matter, of course, they don't know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，真相当然是，他们根本不知道。

sentences.en: They don't speak the language.
sentences.zh: 他们不会说当地语言。

sentences.en: They're entirely reliant on Malinche, this former slave girl, to translate for them.
sentences.zh: 他们完全依赖玛琳切，这个曾是奴隶的女孩来为他们翻译。

sentences.en: But actually, I think in the first few days, they're probably quite relieved because they have servants to wait on them.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，我认为在最初的几天里，他们可能觉得如释重负，因为有仆人伺候他们。

sentences.en: Bernal Diaz,
sentences.zh: 贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯——

sentences.en: you know, all these sources are very suspect, but he's our best source.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有这些史料都非常可疑，但他是我们最好的信源。

sentences.en: And he sort of says, you know, there are people there with tortillas and with bits of turkey and chocolate and corn and these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他大致说过，那里的人们会送上玉米饼、火鸡肉、巧克力、玉米以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And actually, it's fine.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一切都很好。

sentences.en: I mean, you say they don't know what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你刚才说他们不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: Important to emphasize at this point that actually historians can't be certain what's going on as well.
sentences.zh: 此时有必要强调的是，实际上历史学家们也无法确定当时到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: So this is a further dimension to the mystery, as we will come to, that actually the sources for this are treacherous in so many ways.
sentences.zh: 所以这是这个谜团的另一个维度，正如我们接下来要谈到的，这些历史记载在诸多方面都充满了背叛与虚假。

sentences.en: Very treacherous.
sentences.zh: 非常不可靠。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And as a result, there are actually lots of quite opposed theories as to what happens in the days and then the weeks and months that follow.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于接下来的几天、几周和几个月里究竟发生了什么，存在着许多截然相反的学说。

sentences.en: So we should look at that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该探讨一下这个问题。

sentences.en: But I think one thing that is absolutely clear is that the Spaniards would have been completely blown away.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有一点是绝对清楚的，那就是西班牙人绝对被震撼到了。

sentences.en: I mean, we keep harking back to science fiction.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们总是忍不住联想到科幻小说。

sentences.en: This is the equivalent to Captain Kirk beaming down and finding himself in the middle of some spectacular galactic space scape.
sentences.zh: 这就相当于柯克船长使用传送光束降落，发现自己身处某种壮丽的银河太空奇景之中。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Except that, you know, it's on the face of the earth.
sentences.zh: 只不过，你知道的，这是在地球上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They crossed the oceans and found this stunning, stunning city.
sentences.zh: 他们跨越大洋，发现了这座令人惊叹、叹为观止的城市。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're right.
sentences.zh: 对，你说得对。

sentences.en: The science fiction parallel is a good one because so much science fiction is clearly based on these sort of European encounters with indigenous people.
sentences.zh: 用科幻小说来做类比很贴切，因为许多科幻小说显然都是基于欧洲人与原住民遭遇的这类经历创作的。

sentences.en: The remarkable thing is that, as we said before, the Aztec or the Mexica civilization is, what would you call it, Tom, a kind of Bronze Age civilization, I suppose?
sentences.zh: 非同寻常的是，正如我们之前所说，阿兹特克或墨西加文明，你觉得应该叫什么，汤姆，某种青铜时代文明吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They don't have steel swords.
sentences.zh: 他们没有钢剑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They're about the level of what?
sentences.zh: 他们的水平大概相当于什么？

sentences.en: Camilla Tenzin compares it to the Sumerians.
sentences.zh: 卡米拉·坚赞把它比作苏美尔人。

sentences.en: The Sumerians, yeah.
sentences.zh: 苏美尔人，对。

sentences.en: So it's kind of the early Mesopotamian civilizations.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像早期的美索不达米亚文明。

sentences.en: So it's a sophisticated urban civilization, but technologically it is, as it were, if you want to think of it this way, behind the old world.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个高度发达的城市文明，但从技术上讲，如果你愿意这样认为的话，它落后于旧世界。

sentences.en: And yet, Tenochtitlan is a much bigger city than anything they have seen in Europe.
sentences.zh: 然而，特诺奇蒂特兰比他们在欧洲见过的任何城市都要大得多。

sentences.en: As we were saying before, the sort of metro area has probably got a million people in it.
sentences.zh: 正如我们刚才所说，其大都市区可能有一百万人口。

sentences.en: It's also, they say straight away, it's astonishing to them how well ordered, how regimented, how well maintained, how clean.
sentences.zh: 他们还马上提到，这座城市井然有序、纪律严明、维护得当且极其干净，这让他们感到震惊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because it's new, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为它是新建的，对吧？

sentences.en: So unlike, you know, Rome or Paris, where the streets have grown up over many, many centuries, this is much more like an American city, a modern American city,
sentences.zh: 所以不像罗马或巴黎那样，街道是在漫长的岁月中自然生长出来的，这座城市更像是一座美国城市，一座现代美国城市，

sentences.en: kind of grid systems and laid out like that.
sentences.zh: 有着某种网格状的布局。

sentences.en: It has shops though, which American cities, of course, don't, if you're grounded out to
sentences.zh: 不过它有商店，而美国城市当然没有，如果你去过

sentences.en: American shops.
sentences.zh: 美国的商店的话。

sentences.en: So it doesn't have shopping malls, although it does have floating gardens, which is nice.
sentences.zh: 所以它没有大型购物中心，但它有漂浮花园，这很不错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think, I suppose the difference, it's not as chaotic as it, as a European city, as Seville, where many of them would have sailed from.
sentences.zh: 我想，两者的区别在于，它没有欧洲城市那么混乱，比如塞维利亚，他们当中许多人就是从那里启航的。

sentences.en: You know, Seville is an old city and had recently, relatively recently anyway, been retaken from the Moors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，塞维利亚是一座古城，不久前（无论如何也是相对近期）才从摩尔人手中夺回。

sentences.en: So there's a jumble of different influences in Seville, whereas somewhere like Tenochtitlan is probably much more uniform.
sentences.zh: 所以塞维利亚有着各种杂糅的文化影响，而像特诺奇蒂特兰这样的大都市可能要统一得多。

sentences.en: You've got the great pyramids, but also it's so regimented.
sentences.zh: 这里有宏伟的金字塔，而且布局极其规整。

sentences.en: So it's divided into quadrants and each quadrant is divided into neighborhoods and there are different kinds of officials who supervise the
sentences.zh: 它被划分为四个象限，每个象限又细分为各个街区，有不同类型的官员来监管

sentences.en: different neighborhoods and things, and everybody has their place.
sentences.zh: 不同的街区等等，每个人都有自己的位置。

sentences.en: And to go against the expectations of society, of your world, is kind of unthinkable.
sentences.zh: 违背社会和自己世界的期望，简直是不可想象的。

sentences.en: There's no evidence that people really did it.
sentences.zh: 没有证据表明人们真的会这么做。

sentences.en: And in a sense, I think, even though it's a sort of Bronze Age civilization, it clearly is a very powerful apparatus of kind of state regimentation.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，我认为，尽管它某种程度上属于青铜时代文明，但它显然拥有一套非常强大的国家体制管控机器。

sentences.en: So they go, for example, to this huge market at
sentences.zh: 例如，他们去了一个巨大的市场，位于

sentences.en: Tlatelolco, which is another island kind of connected with Tenochtitlan, like a kind of suburb, basically.
sentences.zh: 特拉特洛尔科，那是另一个与特诺奇蒂特兰相连的岛屿，基本上就像一个郊区。

sentences.en: And they go to the market where you can buy everything.
sentences.zh: 他们去了那个应有尽有的市场。

sentences.en: You know, you can buy all these amazing things that they've never seen before, the chocolate and the spices and chilies and feathers, quatzo feathers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可以买到所有这些他们从未见过的神奇东西，巧克力、香料、辣椒和羽毛，珍贵的绿咬鹃羽毛。

sentences.en: Right, exactly, feathers and all these things.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实是羽毛以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: But Bernal Diaz says the thing that really is striking to them is how regimented it is, how well-ordered, how there were officials
sentences.zh: 但贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯说，真正令他们震惊的是这里的秩序井然、管理规范，到处都有官员

sentences.en: everywhere to sort of regulate the weights and measures and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 四处监管度量衡以及所有这类事情。

sentences.en: And this is very Moctezuma, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这非常符合蒙特苏马的作风，对吧？

sentences.en: He seems to have been very into this, the idea that this state that has emerged very, very recently should be set on a firm organizational footing.
sentences.zh: 他似乎非常热衷于此，坚信这个刚刚崛起不久的国家应该建立在牢固的组织基础之上。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So there's that, that amazes them.
sentences.zh: 所以，正是这一点让他们惊叹不已。

sentences.en: But also, as you say, the sheer science fiction kind of culture shock.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，还有那种纯粹的科幻式文化冲击。

sentences.en: So Cortez says in one of his letters at one point, it was all so wondrous that we could barely believe it.
sentences.zh: 因此，科尔特斯在他的信中曾写道：“这一切都太奇妙了，我们简直难以置信。”

sentences.en: Another of his comrades says the city was a place of enchantment.
sentences.zh: 他的另一个同伴说，这座城市是一个充满魔力的地方。

sentences.en: We were never sure whether it was real or if we were dreaming.
sentences.zh: 我们从来不确定它是真的，还是我们在做梦。

sentences.en: And as we said before, they've come having read all these chivalric romances, and suddenly they're in one.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前所说，他们带着读过的所有骑士传奇来到这里，而突然之间，他们就置身于其中了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I suppose the equivalent is like an astronaut who's grown up with Star Wars and Star Trek and all of these things.
sentences.zh: 我想这就好比一个伴随着《星球大战》、《星际迷航》以及所有这些作品长大的宇航员，

sentences.en: Yeah, suddenly.
sentences.zh: 突然之间——

sentences.en: And then he lands on an alien planet and it's just like, you know, there are people with three heads and kind of bustling bazaars and amazing towers and things.
sentences.zh: 然后他降落在一个外星球上，那里有人长着三个脑袋，有熙熙攘攘的集市和令人惊叹的高塔之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think that that kind of sense the Spaniards convey of entering a dreamscape hangs over the whole historiography of it as well.
sentences.zh: 我认为西班牙人所传达的那种进入幻境般的感觉，也笼罩了关于这段历史的所有史学研究。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because the sense of the greatest culture clash, perhaps in the history of human civilization, it's difficult for all of us to get a handle on.
sentences.zh: 因为人类文明史上或许最伟大的文化冲突所带来的那种震撼，对我们所有人来说都很难真正把握。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because it's gone.
sentences.zh: 因为它已经不复存在了。

sentences.en: Tenochtitlan has gone.
sentences.zh: 特诺奇蒂特兰已经消失了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so it's difficult for us to get back to a sense of what it must have been like.
sentences.zh: 所以我们很难再去体会当时的情景到底是怎样的。

sentences.en: And the only way that we can really do it is through the eyes of the Spaniards.
sentences.zh: 我们唯一能真正做到这一点的途径，就是通过西班牙人的眼睛。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Because the Spaniards are the embodiment of the culture that is coming.
sentences.zh: 因为西班牙人就是即将到来的那种文化的化身。

sentences.en: And the most arresting moment from Bernal Diaz's account of these early days is when they go to the Great Temple.
sentences.zh: 在贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯关于这段早期日子的记述中，最引人注目的时刻是他们前往大神庙的时候。

sentences.en: Now you said Tenochtitlan is gone, but I was in Mexico City earlier this year and went to the Great Temple.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说特诺奇蒂特兰已经消失了，但我今年早些时候去过墨西哥城，还参观了大神庙。

sentences.en: The ruins of the Great Temple is still, even the ruins are a remarkable historical site.
sentences.zh: 大神庙的遗址至今——即使只是废墟，也是一个非凡的历史遗迹。

sentences.en: And I have to say the museum is brilliant, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我必须说，那个博物馆太棒了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 绝对太棒了。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Bernal Diaz's account of when they go to that temple.
sentences.zh: 还有贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯关于他们去那座神庙的记述。

sentences.en: I mean, unlike me, they don't know what to expect.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，和我不一样，他们根本不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: You know, I'd been primed for it for years of reading about the Aztecs since I was a little boy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我从小读了多年关于阿兹特克人的书，对此早有心理准备。

sentences.en: They're not primed at all.
sentences.zh: 而他们一点心理准备都没有。

sentences.en: The sheer size of it, I think 114 steps and this sort of stepped pyramid.
sentences.zh: 它的规模之大，我想有114级台阶，这是一座这种阶梯式的金字塔。

sentences.en: They go up to the top.
sentences.zh: 他们一直爬到顶端。

sentences.en: And one of the early afternoons is Montezuma's officials who lead Cortez and his men up to the top.
sentences.zh: 那是某天下午早些时候，蒙特苏马的官员带领科尔特斯和他的手下登上了山顶。

sentences.en: The emperor is already up there sort of doing some sacrifices or whatever.
sentences.zh: 皇帝已经在上面进行某种祭祀活动了。

sentences.en: So they go up there to the 114th step.
sentences.zh: 于是他们一路登上了第114级台阶。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can sort of imagine the scene that they now have the view of the whole city, of the lake.
sentences.zh: 而且，你可以想象当时的场景，他们现在可以俯瞰整座城市和湖泊的全景。

sentences.en: They can see the order of it.
sentences.zh: 他们能看到这里的秩序。

sentences.en: They can see the size.
sentences.zh: 他们能看到它的规模。

sentences.en: Just an incredible scene.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个令人难以置信的场面。

sentences.en: Bernal Diaz says some of his companions who had been to Constantinople and Rome and traveled through the whole of Italy.
sentences.zh: 贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯说，他的一些同伴曾去过君士坦丁堡和罗马，游历过整个意大利。

sentences.en: Of course, they've traveled through Italy because they've probably been mercenaries or merchants or they've been involved in the many Italian wars in the early 16th century.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们游历过意大利，因为他们可能当过雇佣兵或商人，或者卷入了16世纪初的多次意大利战争。

sentences.en: And they say, God, this is incredible.
sentences.zh: 他们说：“天哪，这太不可思议了。”

sentences.en: You know, I've never been anywhere like this.
sentences.zh: “我从没去过这样地方。”

sentences.en: But then there's this absolutely
sentences.zh: 但随后出现了这样一个

sentences.en: extraordinary culture clash scene, if you believe Bernal Diaz's account.
sentences.zh: 极其震撼的文化冲突场景，如果你相信贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯的记述的话。

sentences.zh: 有个关于他们玩一种叫托托洛克（Totoloque）的游戏的传说，基本上就是你扔一些小圆球去击中一根金条。

sentences.en: Gold bar, I mean, they must have loved seeing that.
sentences.zh: 金条，我的意思是，他们看到这个一定爱不释手。

sentences.en: And Cortez's sort of comrade, Pedro de Alvarado, the story is that he offers to keep the score as Cortez plays the emperor.
sentences.zh: 据说科尔特斯的战友佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多在科尔特斯与皇帝对弈时主动提出负责记分。

sentences.en: But Alvarado is a cheat.
sentences.zh: 但阿尔瓦拉多是个老千。

sentences.en: He keeps inflating Cortez's score because he wants the Spanish to win.
sentences.zh: 他不断夸大科尔特斯的分数，因为他想让西班牙人赢。

sentences.en: That's not cricket.
sentences.zh: 这可真不地道。

sentences.en: And Montezuma notices and says, don't think I can't see what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 蒙特苏马注意到了，并说道，别以为我不知道你在干什么。

sentences.en: You're trying to cheat in this game.
sentences.zh: 你想在这个游戏里出老千。

sentences.en: And there's also a story that the emperor took a shine to one of Cortez's page boys.
sentences.zh: 还有一个故事说，皇帝看上了科尔特斯的一个男侍从。

sentences.en: I'm guessing it's probably a teenager called Juan Orteguia.
sentences.zh: 我猜那可能是一个叫胡安·奥特吉亚的少年。

sentences.en: And he teaches him some
sentences.zh: 他教了他一些

sentences.en: Nahuatl and Orteguia, tells him stories about life in Spain.
sentences.zh: 纳瓦特尔语，而奥特吉亚则给他讲了西班牙的生活故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We have this thing called Tapas.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种叫塔帕斯的食物。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 原来如此。

sentences.en: That's what he said, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他就是这么说的，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I think that's very plausible.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这非常合乎情理。

sentences.en: They also do have little sort of jaunts, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们也经常一起进行一些短途游玩，对吧？

sentences.en: They go kind of hawking and they go hunting.
sentences.zh: 他们会去进行类似鹰猎和狩猎的活动。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, Dominic, you go abroad, you want to go on a jaunt, don't you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，多米尼克，你出国去玩，就是想出去游玩一番，对吧？

sentences.en: You do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: You want a guided tour and you want a jaunt.
sentences.zh: 你想参加导游团，也想出去观光游玩。

sentences.en: I know you love a jaunt.
sentences.zh: 我知道你很喜欢出去游玩。

sentences.en: Well, I like a jaunt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我是挺喜欢游玩的。

sentences.en: I don't love a guided tour, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢有导游带领的旅行，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think that's where you and I,
sentences.zh: 我想这就是你和我的分歧所在，

sentences.en: it's one of the great cleavages in the rest of this history, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这也是本历史节目余下部分中最大的分歧之一，对吧？

sentences.en: You love a guided tour.
sentences.zh: 你很喜欢导游团。

sentences.en: I don't really like guided tours because I like to do my own thing.
sentences.zh: 我其实不太喜欢导游团，因为我喜欢做自己想做的事。

sentences.en: Because you are the cat that walks alone.
sentences.zh: 因为你是那只独来独往的猫。

sentences.en: I am the cat, but I do like a day trip.
sentences.zh: 我是那只猫，但我确实喜欢一日游。

sentences.en: And they do go on day trips to the sort of lakeshore and they go hunting and things.
sentences.zh: 他们确实会去湖岸之类的地方进行一日游，还会去打猎什么的。

sentences.en: And the most extraordinary thing, which historians have puzzled over, is they undoubtedly build ships.
sentences.zh: 最离奇的是，这也是让历史学家们百思不得其解的地方，他们毫无疑问建造了船只。

sentences.en: So they show off that they can build these ships.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在炫耀自己能够建造这些船只。

sentences.en: He must have heard about their extraordinary naval technology, extraordinary to the Mexica.
sentences.zh: 他一定听说过他们非凡的海军技术，对墨西加人来说这简直非同寻常。

sentences.en: They build some ships with room for cannons and things.
sentences.zh: 他们建造了一些配有加农炮等设施的船只。

sentences.en: Now, is that them showing off or is that them doing a job for him?
sentences.zh: 那么，这到底是他们在炫耀，还是他们在为他办事？

sentences.en: Well, so this is the question, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以这就是问题所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, who is in control of who at this point?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，此时究竟是谁在控制谁？

sentences.en: That's the key.
sentences.zh: 这才是关键。

sentences.en: Here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 关键在于：

sentences.en: Is he their plaything or are they his?
sentences.zh: 他是他们的玩物，还是他们是他的玩物？

sentences.en: Are they his guests?
sentences.zh: 他们是他的客人吗？

sentences.en: Are they his prisoners?
sentences.zh: 他们是他的囚犯吗？

sentences.en: Is he their prisoner?
sentences.zh: 他是他们的囚犯吗？

sentences.en: This is the great...
sentences.zh: 这是个巨大的……

sentences.en: Or are they perhaps animals in his zoo, which is a brilliant recent theory that perhaps we should
sentences.zh: 或者他们也许是他动物园里的动物——这是一个非常精彩的最新理论，也许我们应该

sentences.en: come to after the break when we discuss exactly, you know, who is exploiting who at this point?
sentences.zh: 在休息之后再来讨论，届时我们将具体探讨，你知道的，此时究竟是谁在剥削谁？

sentences.en: Very much debated.
sentences.zh: 这争论非常激烈。

sentences.en: So we will be back in a few minutes to discuss that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将在几分钟后回来讨论这个问题。

sentences.zh: 那架载有350名乘客的航班。

sentences.zh: 伟大博弈。

sentences.zh: 我们来评估一下我们的首相。

sentences.en: With high confidence it was Russian.
sentences.zh: 我们高度确信那是俄罗斯干的。

sentences.zh: 追究俄罗斯人的责任就等于第三次世界大战。

sentences.zh: 他们击落了一架载有350人的英国客机。

sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫的那个人在玩手段，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: You've got to ask yourself, do you want to play or not?
sentences.zh: 你得问问自己，你到底想不想陪他玩。

sentences.zh: 你却什么都……

sentences.zh: 什么都没做！

sentences.zh: 我们需要了解政策背景。

sentences.zh: 或者是一条要求……的作战指令，

sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到《历史就是力量》（The Rest is History）。

sentences.en: We are in Tenochtitlan with Moctezuma and Cortez.
sentences.zh: 我们正身处特诺奇蒂特兰，与蒙特苏马和科尔特斯在一起。

sentences.en: And Dominic, before the break, we were discussing who exactly has the whip hand at this moment.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，在休息之前，我们一直在讨论此时究竟谁占据着绝对的主动权。

sentences.en: I mean, Moctezuma, presumably.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大概是蒙特苏马吧。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, he's the emperor.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，他是皇帝。

sentences.en: He's the ruler of a vast empire.
sentences.zh: 他是一个庞大帝国的统治者。

sentences.en: But Cortez is a figure so alarming, I think, to Moctezuma that he hasn't done the obvious thing and tried to have the Spaniards killed.
sentences.zh: 但科尔特斯在蒙特苏马看来是一个如此令人惊恐的人物，以至于他没有做那件显而易见的事——试图派人杀死西班牙人。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's, I mean, that's the dog that doesn't bark in the night, really.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这其实就是那个“夜半没有狗叫”的谜题。

sentences.en: But I suppose you would say, Tom, why would he have them killed?
sentences.zh: 但我想你会说，汤姆，他为什么要派人杀了他们呢？

sentences.en: So, in other words, to use your science fiction analogy,
sentences.zh: 所以，换句话说，借用你的科幻小说类比，

sentences.en: if aliens landed on our planet with tremendous technology and there were 300 of them and they arrived in Washington DC or in London or Paris or whatever,
sentences.zh: 如果有外星人带着极其先进的技术降临我们的星球，他们有300人，抵达了华盛顿特区、伦敦或巴黎等地，

sentences.en: would your instinct be to kill them?
sentences.zh: 你的第一直觉会是杀死他们吗？

sentences.en: I think your instinct would be to treat them with extreme nervousness, to try and find out what their technology was, to find out exactly what they can do, how dangerous are they?
sentences.zh: 我想你的直觉应该是对他们保持极度的警惕，试图了解他们的技术是什么，弄清楚他们到底能做什么，他们有多危险？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And to try and work out how many more of them are lurking in the background.
sentences.zh: 并试图弄清楚暗中还有多少这样的外星人潜伏着。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, in other words, if I kill all the aliens, is there an entire fleet of flying saucers waiting to come in?
sentences.zh: 所以，换句话说，如果我把所有的外星人都杀了，会不会有一整支飞碟舰队正等待着开过来呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, those would be the two things that I would want to do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这会是我想要做的两件事。

sentences.en: And you were saying about how Cortez develops a ship.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到科尔特斯是如何建造一艘船的。

sentences.en: I mean, this is obviously of interest in Moctezuma, but it is also Cortez's way of demonstrating, if we can build a ship like this,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这显然会让蒙特苏马感兴趣，但这也是科尔特斯的一种展示方式：如果我们能建造这样一艘船，

sentences.en: then think how many of us can come across the Great Ocean.
sentences.zh: 那么想想看，我们有多少人能横渡大洋来到这里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that's very plausible.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常合乎情理。

sentences.en: I mean, I think another way of thinking about it is this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为还有另一种思考方式。

sentences.en: Imagine if people with 19th century technology had pitched up in 15th century England, the time of the Wars of the Roses.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果拥有19世纪技术的人出现在15世纪的英格兰，也就是玫瑰战争时期。

sentences.en: So, a period we know a fair amount about.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们相当了解的时期。

sentences.en: We know how people thought.
sentences.zh: 我们了解当时人们的想法。

sentences.en: We know what kind of assumptions Edward IV and Richard III and people like that had.
sentences.zh: 我们知道爱德华四世、理查三世之流有着什么样的假设。

sentences.en: Is it plausible that if Captain Cook or David Livingstone or General Gordon had arrived, that they would have been killed immediately?
sentences.zh: 如果库克船长、大卫·利文斯顿或戈登将军抵达那里，他们会被立刻杀死吗？这合理吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: People would have been absolutely fascinated, as I'm sure the Mexica were.
sentences.zh: 人们会感到绝对的着迷，就像我确信墨西加人当时那样。

sentences.en: What I don't think is plausible is that the hosts in that situation just completely abased themselves and groveled.
sentences.zh: 我认为不合情理的是，那种情况下的主人竟然完全自轻自贱、卑躬屈膝。

sentences.en: Now, that is the image that you get in the Spanish sources and in the kind of orthodox histories of the conquest of Mexico that so many of our listeners would have read,
sentences.zh: 而这正是你在西班牙史料以及关于征服墨西哥的正统历史中所看到的形象，我们的许多听众都曾读过这些内容，

sentences.en: probably when they were children or teenagers or something.
sentences.zh: 可能是在他们还是儿童或青少年的时候。

sentences.en: Because this is the claim that Cortez makes, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为这就是科尔特斯所声称的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Writing shortly after to the king, saying that Moctezuma, the first thing he's done is essentially surrender his kingdom to the Spanish king.
sentences.zh: 他不久后给国王写信称，蒙特苏马做的第一件事基本上就是向西班牙国王投降他的王国。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, in Cortez's account, in the standard account, Montezuma surrendered his kingdom almost immediately, you know, within hours of their arrival.
sentences.zh: 因此，在科尔特斯的叙述中，在标准叙述中，蒙特苏马几乎在他们抵达后的几小时内就投降了他的王国，

sentences.en: And said, I am the vassal of Charles V.
sentences.zh: 并说，我是查理五世的臣属。

sentences.en: You know, my kingdom now belongs to you.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的王国现在属于你们了。

sentences.en: And obviously, this then was layered over with all the stuff about him thinking they're gods and all this business, which I think is clearly not true.
sentences.zh: 显然，这后来又被加上了各种关于他认为他们是神明之类的说辞，我认为这显然不是真的。

sentences.en: And then, in the standard account, quite soon, they decide they'll actually take him prisoner and they hold him as a hostage for months and months and months.
sentences.zh: 然后，按照标准的叙述，很快他们就决定将他软禁起来，并把他作为人质扣押了长达数月之久。

sentences.en: But weirdly, he carries on ruling the kingdom, but under their supervision.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的是，他继续统治着王国，只是在他们的监视之下。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in the Spanish accounts, they will describe Montezuma going off and doing whatever he likes.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙人的记录中，他们会描述蒙特苏马去办他想办的任何事。

sentences.en: And then suddenly you remember that he's meant to have been a prisoner and try and kind of offer explanations as to how, if he was a prisoner,
sentences.zh: 然后你突然又记起他本该是个囚犯，于是便试图为以下情况提供某种解释：如果他是个囚犯，

sentences.en: he was going off on grand processions and things.
sentences.zh: 他怎么还能去进行盛大的游行活动之类的呢。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: They keep forgetting their story.
sentences.zh: 他们总是忘记自己的故事设定。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, when they're going on the day trips, they say, one day we decided to go, you know, hunting with Montezuma.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他们去进行一日游时，他们会说，有一天我们决定去和蒙特苏马一起，你知道的，去打猎。

sentences.en: He assembled all his men.
sentences.zh: 他召集了他所有的人。

sentences.en: We went off.
sentences.zh: 我们出发了。

sentences.en: He was, of course, still our prisoner.
sentences.zh: 当然，他依然是我们的囚犯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, I mean, the historian who really destroys this is Matthew Restle in his brilliant, brilliant book on the meeting between Montezuma and Cortez.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，真正彻底推翻这一说法的历史学家是马修·雷斯托尔（Matthew Restall），他在那本关于蒙特苏马与科尔特斯会面的精彩绝伦的书中进行了论证。

sentences.en: But even before that, it was an inherently implausible idea that for months and months and months,
sentences.zh: 但即便在此之前，这种说法本身也是极其不合逻辑的：连续好几个月，

sentences.en: the people of Tenochtitlan would just be so passive and traumatized and lacking in agency that they would just sort of plod along to the markets as though nothing had happened.
sentences.zh: 特诺奇蒂特兰的人民怎么会如此被动、受到创伤且缺乏自主性，以至于他们只是像什么都没发生过一样继续机械地去集市呢？

sentences.en: While their emperor was being held prisoner.
sentences.zh: 而他们的皇帝当时正被当做人质扣押着。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's true that the Spanish are well armed.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人确实武装精良，这也是事实。

sentences.en: It's also true they had the Tlaxcalan allies.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有特拉斯卡拉人作为盟友也是事实。

sentences.en: But I would assume that at some stage the Tlaxcalans must have gone home.
sentences.zh: 但我猜想特拉斯卡拉人在某个阶段一定回家了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because they're a very mysterious presence in the whole story we were talking about in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在上一集中谈到，他们在整个故事中是一个非常神秘的存在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's unclear what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚他们在做什么。

sentences.en: There aren't thousands of them billeted in the city for months and months and months.
sentences.zh: 并没有成千上万的人在城里驻扎好几个月。

sentences.en: There's no reference to that actually in the sources.
sentences.zh: 史料中其实并没有相关的记载。

sentences.en: So I think at some point they must have gone home.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们在某个时刻一定回去了。

sentences.en: The Spanish, of course, they're formidable.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人当然很强大。

sentences.en: But, you know, if the Wagner group descended on London, took Rishi Sunak hostage and holed up in Whitehall, it's utterly implausible for nine months or something.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，如果瓦格纳集团降临伦敦，把里希·苏纳克劫为人质并固守在白厅，长达九个月左右都毫无营救举动，这简直是完全不合情理的。

sentences.en: Yeah, no attempt would be made to get him back.
sentences.zh: 对，不会有人试图去把他救回来。

sentences.en: No attempt would be made to rescue him.
sentences.zh: 不会有人去试图营救他。

sentences.en: There wouldn't be some uprising.
sentences.zh: 也不会发生任何起义。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just utterly unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: So the question is, as the sort of New Conquest historians say, the question is what is going on?
sentences.zh: 所以正如“新征服史”历史学家所说，问题在于这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And Matthew Restall has this absolutely fascinating argument that all the stories about them being Montezuma's guards and him being the prisoner is actually a massive exercise in projection and that they really are his prisoners.
sentences.zh: 马修·雷斯托尔提出了一个绝对引人入胜的论点：所有关于他们是蒙特苏马的卫兵、他是囚犯的故事，实际上是一场大规模的投射演练，而他们实际上才是他的囚犯。

sentences.en: And he has them under guard in that palace, that they are probably at his beck and call.
sentences.zh: 他在那座宫殿里派人看守他们，他们很可能随叫随到。

sentences.en: And that's because he has a very, very specific fate in mind for them.
sentences.zh: 那是因为他为他们准备了一个非常非常特殊的命运。

sentences.en: Because we mentioned that one of the things he showed them was his zoo.
sentences.zh: 因为我们提到过，他向他们展示的东西之一就是他的动物园。

sentences.en: And Montezuma is very unusual in having a zoo at all because European monarchs didn't have zoos.
sentences.zh: 蒙特苏马拥有动物园是非常罕见的，因为欧洲君主并没有动物园。

sentences.en: Is that right, Tom?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: So we talked about this, I think, in a previous episode about the zoo in the Tower of London and zoo very loosely.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们之前在讨论伦敦塔的动物园时谈到过这个，不过“动物园”这个词用得很勉强。

sentences.en: They have wild animals there.
sentences.zh: 他们那里有野生动物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But Montezuma's appetite for collecting seems to have been on an order that would be familiar, say, to Pliny the Elder.
sentences.zh: 但蒙特祖马对收集的嗜好，其规模之大，用老普林尼的话来说，大概会让人觉得很熟悉。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or to the authors of the Encyclopedia Britannica or even to Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 或者跟《大英百科全书》的编者们，甚至维基百科相比。

sentences.en: We've talked about this before,
sentences.zh: 我们以前讨论过这个，

sentences.en: how great empires often express their sense of their universal purpose and destiny with a mania for collecting and tabulating and constructing encyclopedias or even better constructing great museums or zoos.
sentences.zh: 伟大的帝国如何常常通过一种收集、分类和编写百科全书的狂热，来表达他们对自身普世目标和命运的感知，或者更好的是，建造伟大的博物馆或动物园。

sentences.en: And this is what Montezuma is evidently doing.
sentences.zh: 而这显然就是蒙特祖马在做的事。

sentences.en: And it's such a brilliant theory.
sentences.zh: 这是一个多么精妙的理论啊。

sentences.en: And I gather, I listened to Matthew Restyl being interviewed, that he was reading a thesis by a Mexican scholar.
sentences.zh: 据我了解——我听了马修·雷斯托尔的采访——他当时正在读一位墨西哥学者的论文。

sentences.en: So it hadn't been translated into English.
sentences.zh: 所以这篇论文还没有被翻译成英文。

sentences.en: And this was all about Montezuma and his mania for collecting.
sentences.zh: 内容全是关于蒙特祖马和他收集的狂热。

sentences.en: And he was so impressed by it that he got in touch with the scholar and then married her.
sentences.zh: 他对此印象深刻，于是联系了这位学者，后来还娶了她。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，对。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's a lovely detail.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个可爱的细节。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Great detail, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 很棒的细节，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's very Somerton Man.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合萨默顿先生案的风格。

sentences.en: That's what happened in the Somerton Man story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 萨默顿先生的故事里就是这么发生的，对吧？

sentences.en: The investigator married one of them.
sentences.zh: 调查员娶了其中一位当事人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To a degree.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上。

sentences.en: To a degree.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上。

sentences.en: So that will mean nothing to people who haven't heard Tom's brilliant, brilliant true crime podcast about the greatest mystery in Australian history.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于没有听过汤姆关于澳大利亚历史上最大谜团的那档精彩绝伦的真实犯罪播客的人来说，这话完全听不懂。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以这么说，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Montezuma Zoo, there's a royal judge later on, a Spanish judge called Alonso Zuazo.
sentences.zh: 所以蒙特祖马动物园——后来有一位皇家法官，一位名叫阿隆索·苏瓦索的西班牙法官。

sentences.en: And he spoke to the conquistadors.
sentences.zh: 他与征服者们交谈过。

sentences.en: And he later recorded Montezuma had for show a house in which he had a great diversity of serpents and wild animals, which included tigers, bears, lions.
sentences.zh: 他后来记载道，蒙特祖马展示过一个宅邸，里面有各种各样形形色色的蛇类和野生动物，其中包括老虎、熊、狮子。

sentences.en: By the way, spoiler.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，剧透一下。

sentences.en: He definitely didn't have tigers and lions, did he, Tom?
sentences.zh: 他绝对没有老虎和狮子，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Wild boar, vipers, rattlesnakes, toads, frogs, many other snakes and birds, right down to worMs.
sentences.zh: 野猪、毒蛇、响尾蛇、蟾蜍、青蛙、许多其他的蛇和鸟类，甚至一直到各种虫子。

sentences.en: And each one of these things was in its place and in cages as needed.
sentences.zh: 而且这些东西每一件都各得其所，根据需要关在笼子里。

sentences.en: So that's the classification mania, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是分类狂热，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: With people assigned to give them food and all that was necessary to take care of them.
sentences.zh: 有人专门负责给它们喂食以及照顾它们所需的一切。

sentences.en: Now, here's the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，有趣的地方来了。

sentences.en: He also had other people that were monstrous, such as dwarves and hunchbacks, some with one arm and others that were missing a leg and other monstrous races that are born as such.
sentences.zh: 他身边还有一些奇形怪状的人，比如侏儒和驼背，有的人只有一只胳膊，有的少了一条腿，还有天生就是这样的其他奇异人种。

sentences.en: So in other words, like so many monarchs, like Peter the Great or something, Montezuma is fascinated by people who are different.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就像许多君主一样，比如彼得大帝之类，蒙特祖马对与众不同的人着迷。

sentences.en: So the hunchbacks or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以就是驼背之类的人。

sentences.en: And as Matthew Restall says, it's perfectly plausible that an emperor who wants to collect everything because that will show he has power.
sentences.zh: 正如马修·雷斯托尔所说，一个渴望收集一切的皇帝，这种想法完全合乎情理，因为这能证明他拥有权力。

sentences.en: He has dominion over flora, fauna and all the different peoples.
sentences.zh: 他统治着动植物以及所有不同的人群。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's the same thing as beasts in the arena.
sentences.zh: 这跟竞技场里的野兽是同一个道理。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: In Rome.
sentences.zh: 在罗马。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's a display of the global reach of the emperor.
sentences.zh: 这是对皇帝全球势力范围的一种展示。

sentences.en: It's perfectly plausible that he would see the arrival of these extraordinary new people as a chance to add to his collection.
sentences.zh: 他把这些非凡新面孔的到来视为扩充自己收藏的机会，这是完全合乎情理的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's obviously not going to stick them in cages, you know, like they're at Chester Zoo or something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他显然不会把他们塞进笼子里，你知道的，就像他们是在切斯特动物园或者别的地方一样。

sentences.en: But it's telling that the place where he houses them, the palace of Aksaya cattle, is very close to the zoo complex.
sentences.zh: 但耐人寻味的是，他安置他们的住所——阿萨亚卡特尔宫，距离动物园综合区非常近。

sentences.en: So he might be sort of thinking, well, it would be great to have this addition.
sentences.zh: 所以他可能在想，嗯，能有这样的新添置会很棒。

sentences.en: These people who work for me, who are my play things.
sentences.zh: 这些人，他们为我工作，是我的玩物。

sentences.en: And also the fact they're armed, they're technologically adept.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还带着武器，精通技术，这也是一个事实。

sentences.en: He might also be thinking they make great bodyguards.
sentences.zh: 他可能也在想，他们能成为很棒的保镖。

sentences.en: But he's clearly never watched Jurassic Park.
sentences.zh: 但他显然没看过《侏罗纪公园》。

sentences.en: No, he hasn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没看过。

sentences.en: Spanish park, conquistador park.
sentences.zh: 西班牙公园，征服者公园。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, if that's what he's doing and he thinks that he can keep them safely in their complex, I mean, obviously they're going to break out and run amok.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的意思是，如果这就是他正在做的，并且他认为自己可以把他们安全地关在他们的区域里——我的意思是，他们显然会爆发并大肆破坏。

sentences.en: But the thought that they would become a kind of elite guard.
sentences.zh: 但他们会成为某种精锐卫队的想法……

sentences.en: See, I'm reminded of Roman emperors, Tom Caligula.
sentences.zh: 你看，这让我想起了罗马皇帝，汤姆，卡利古拉。

sentences.en: He had a group called the Germans, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 他有一个叫日耳曼卫队的群体，对吧？

sentences.en: The Batavians.
sentences.zh: 巴达维亚人。

sentences.en: Yeah, they were Batavians.
sentences.zh: 对，他们是巴达维亚人。

sentences.en: And the Varangians in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 还有君士坦丁堡的瓦兰吉亚卫队。

sentences.en: Well, we've done podcasts about Baghdad, haven't we?
sentences.zh: 我们做过关于巴格达的播客，对吧？

sentences.en: So the Abbasid caliphate, they employed slave soldiers as an elite guard.
sentences.zh: 所以阿拔斯王朝，他们雇佣奴隶士兵作为精锐卫队。

sentences.en: The Mamlu, you know, in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，埃及的马穆鲁克。

sentences.en: And this, of course, is what the Clash of Carlons are after as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是卡隆冲突的目标所在。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess it's kind of competitive tendering.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我猜这有点像竞争性投标。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Whoever can get the Spaniards on their side.
sentences.zh: 谁能把西班牙人拉拢到自己这边。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But obviously, from Moctezuma's point of view, they have to be subordinate to him.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，从蒙特祖马的角度来看，他们必须臣服于他。

sentences.en: And that is not at all what the Spaniards think.
sentences.zh: 而这绝对不是西班牙人的想法。

sentences.en: So there's an inherent tension there.
sentences.zh: 所以其中存在着一种固有的紧张关系。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because they behave badly, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的行为很恶劣，我觉得这么说很公平。

sentences.en: The Spaniards.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm guessing that these months are a process of both sides trying to work out what the measure is of the other.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我猜这几个月是一个过程，双方都在试图摸清对方的底细。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But of course, the Spanish have come there.
sentences.zh: 但当然，西班牙人已经来到了那里。

sentences.en: Most of them, we used the phrase before, Matthew Restor's phrase, armed entrepreneurs.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数人——我们之前用过这个词，马修·雷斯托尔的词汇——武装创业者。

sentences.en: Most of them have come to make money.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数人来是为了赚钱。

sentences.en: That's what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们在做的事。

sentences.en: It's a great adventure, but they're there in the long run to get money, to get gold,
sentences.zh: 这是一场伟大的冒险，但从长远来看，他们去那是为了赚钱，为了黄金，

sentences.en: to improve their status and that of their family and their clan and their patronage network and whatever.
sentences.zh: 为了提升他们自己、他们的家族、他们的宗族以及他们的关系网等等的地位。

sentences.en: And over time, you can well imagine people saying to Cortez, what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，你完全可以想象有人对科尔特斯说，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: We've been here like two and a half months.
sentences.zh: 我们都在这儿待了差不多两个半月了。

sentences.en: And, you know, enough of the kind of going and hawking with the emperor.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，别再跟皇帝一起去打猎了。

sentences.en: When are we going to get the gold and go back?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候才能拿到黄金然后回去？

sentences.en: And there are stories, first of all, that Cortez is constantly pestering Montezuma for more gold, but also stories that some of the Spanish behave badly,
sentences.zh: 有传言说，首先，科尔特斯不断纠缠蒙特祖马索要更多黄金，但也有传言说，一些西班牙人行为恶劣，

sentences.en: that they don't stay in their cage, as it were.
sentences.zh: 他们没有待在所谓的笼子里。

sentences.en: They roam out through the kind of palace complex.
sentences.zh: 他们在宫殿大院里四处闲逛。

sentences.en: They will ransack rooMs.
sentences.zh: 他们会洗劫房间。

sentences.en: They will basically steal fans and feathers and necklaces that they've been heaping up gold and they've even started to melt it down.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上会去偷扇子、羽毛和项链，他们一直在堆积黄金，甚至已经开始把它熔化了。

sentences.en: So there's an advisor in Montezuma who says they've been shouting and quarreling.
sentences.zh: 所以蒙特祖马的一位顾问说，他们一直在大喊大叫、争吵不休。

sentences.en: They seize the treasures as if they were their own, like slaves to their greed.
sentences.zh: 他们夺取珍宝仿佛那是他们自己的东西，就像贪婪的奴隶。

sentences.en: They were laughing like beasts.
sentences.zh: 他们像野兽一样狂笑。

sentences.en: Actually, that comparison with beasts perhaps gives you some sense of how some of Montezuma's people are thinking of them.
sentences.zh: 事实上，与野兽的这种比较，或许能让你对蒙特祖马的一些手下是如何看待他们的有所体会。

sentences.en: And Cortez is already muttering about building ships and presumably he wants to build ships, more ships, because he knows he might be stopped on the causeway.
sentences.zh: 而且科尔特斯已经在嘟囔着要造船了，想必他想要造船，造更多的船，因为他知道自己可能会在堤道上被拦下。

sentences.en: It'd be very helpful for him to have ships to get across the lake.
sentences.zh: 拥有船只对他穿过湖泊会非常有帮助。

sentences.en: And then he's got to think about transporting the gold to the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 然后他还得考虑把黄金运送到海岸。

sentences.en: So one obvious question would be, well, if the Spaniards are causing trouble,
sentences.zh: 所以一个显而易见的问题是，如果西班牙人正在惹麻烦，

sentences.en: if they're clearly not going to be very good as exhibits in a zoo or even effectively employable as bodyguards, what do you do with them?
sentences.zh: 如果他们显然不适合作为动物园里的展品，甚至无法被有效雇用为保镖，你该拿他们怎么办？

sentences.en: And one obvious choice would be to sacrifice them or kill them or have them wiped out.
sentences.zh: 一个显而易见的选择是将他们献祭、杀死或者将其全部消灭。

sentences.en: And sacrificing them might be the best opportunity to keep the gods happy.
sentences.zh: 而把他们献祭可能是让神明保持愉悦的最佳机会。

sentences.en: Oh, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是的。

sentences.en: And it so happens, doesn't it, that winter is turning to spring and that brings a particular month hoving into view.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，不是吗，冬天正转为春天，这就带来了一个特殊的月份进入人们的视野。

sentences.en: And this month has the brilliant name of the flaying of men.
sentences.zh: 这个月有一个绝妙的名字叫“剥人皮之月”。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I know you love this, Tom, because you were very keen when we had a world cup of gods.
sentences.zh: 我知道你很喜欢这个，汤姆，因为当我们举办诸神世界杯时，你表现得非常热心。

sentences.en: So for those people who think this is just Babel, we organized a vote on Twitter and did some podcasts about which was the best god in human history.
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些认为这简直一团糟的人，我们在推特上组织了一场投票，并做了一些播客，探讨谁是人类历史上最棒的神。

sentences.en: You were very keen to see the Mexica god, Chibitotec, thrive.
sentences.zh: 你当时非常热切地希望看到墨西加神——希皮托特克大放异彩。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Our lord, the flayed one.
sentences.zh: 我们的主，剥皮者。

sentences.en: He crashed out in the first round, I'm afraid.
sentences.zh: 恐怕他在第一轮就被淘汰了。

sentences.en: He did very poorly.
sentences.zh: 他表现得很糟糕。

sentences.en: For reasons that may have to do with the general vibe that surrounds his cult.
sentences.zh: 原因可能与围绕他的崇拜的那种总体氛围有关。

sentences.en: So basically, he's the god of fertility.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他是生育之神。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he flays himself to give food to humanity.
sentences.zh: 他剥下自己的皮来为人类提供食物。

sentences.en: And there's this idea of life growing out of the flayed body, which you can kind of see the point of.
sentences.zh: 而且有这样一种理念，即生命从被剥皮的躯体中生长出来，这种逻辑你多少能理解。

sentences.en: But I think to our non-Mashica way of thinking, I think Chippy is the most terrifying of all the gods.
sentences.zh: 但我认为按照我们这种非墨西加的思维方式，我觉得希皮是最可怕的所有神明。

sentences.en: And the festival that's celebrated during the month of the flaying of men, which marks the spring equinox,
sentences.zh: 在剥人皮之月庆祝的节日标志着春分，

sentences.en: the Mexica would get prisoners and they would fight the equivalent of gladiatorial combat.
